title: Lift a heavy two-handled pot with both hands and pour the soup into a bowl
instruction: Lift the pot off the stove by both handles, pour all of the soup into the white bowl without spilling, and set the pot back down on the stove.
context: Serving soup from a full stockpot is a two-handed job at home and in restaurant kitchens: the pot is too heavy to hold by one handle, so both hands must lift, tip and set it down together, steadily enough that nothing spills.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A black round stove block, 16 cm across and 5 cm tall, fixed to the table with its centre 17 cm forward on the centre line. (2) A steel stockpot with straight sides, inside 12 cm across and 13 cm deep (walls 6 mm), 1.0 kg empty, loose, standing centred on the stove. It has two flat upright black lug handles, each 5 cm long, 3 cm tall and 1.2 cm thick, sticking straight out to the left and to the right (toward the two arms), their centres 11.5 cm above the pot's underside. (3) The soup: 90 orange plastic beads 12 mm across, 2 g each, in two layers on the pot's floor. (4) A white straight-sided serving bowl, inside 16 cm across and 8.5 cm deep, fixed to the table with its centre 34 cm forward on the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Counted at the end of the trial, placing each bead by its centre. 0.0 if at any time the pot tilts 30 degrees or more while any part of it is within 6 cm of the table (tipped over on the stove rather than lifted), or if it ends tilted 30 degrees or more. Otherwise 1.0 with at least 77 of the 90 beads in the bowl, at most 4 spilled (outside both the pot and the bowl) and the pot back upright on the stove (tilted less than 10 degrees, its centre within 3 cm of the stove's centre and its underside within 1 cm of the stove's top); 0.5 with at least 45 beads in the bowl and at most 9 spilled; 0.25 with at least 9 in the bowl; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with everything still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: tip the beads from the bowl back into the pot, spread them on its floor, and stand the pot back on the stove with its lugs pointing left and right.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the soup is 90 rigid 12 mm beads standing in for liquid (they pour and roll but do not slosh or splash); the pot's and bowl's round walls are 24 and 20 flat segments; the stove is a plain block; friction is set (pot 0.6, beads 0.3); the cameras render at 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
